Transport setup safeguards & naming audit

Development audit — 5 October 2026. No production writes, no name changes, no merged/deleted/new rate cards. All 11 saved rows in both development targets are byte-for-byte equivalent as JSON before and after, including timestamps; all three setup fields remain NULL. NARASIMHULU: 5 saved cards, 39 screen rows.

Protection implemented

  • Bill write-back uses a legacy-column allowlist. Supplied numeric values AND explicit NULLs for leadDistanceKm, payloadMt, ratePerKm are ignored on both single and bulk upserts.
  • Only the dedicated PATCH /api/vendor-rate-cards/:id/transport-setup accepts basis writes. It retains the existing permission gate: Create on vendor_masters_manage OR admin_settings, with admin/owner bypass.
  • The update matches ID + exact stored itemKey + transport category. No normalization, insert/upsert, name, label, unit, flat-rate, notes or timestamp writes. Missing row returns404; unexpected fields such as itemLabel return400.
  • Setup is disabled for unsaved discovered/manual rows. Existing Add Row/Save All and old bill naming policies were not redesigned; those legacy paths cannot write the new fields.
  • A server cannot prove a request originated from a particular screen: the enforceable boundary is the authenticated, permission-checked, dedicated API, not a spoofable Referer header.

Saved duplicate review — all vendors

One spelling/spacing pair: NARASIMHULU equipment rows74 and76. 2 saved rows; 2 rates set (₹3,000/HRS each). Exact keys appear below. No other spelling/case/spacing-only key pair was identified among the 11 saved development rows.

Additional identity-review candidates, not spelling duplicates: SANGANNA rows5/6 share TIPPER - DAILY HIRE labels but different keys32_DAILY_HIRE /33_DAILY_HIRE and rates₹1,500/₹2,000. MOHAN REDDY rows39/72 have vendor-qualified and generic PAVER FINISHER labels, keys21_DAILY_HIRE /EQ_PAVER_FINISHER_DAYS, rates₹10,500/₹10,000. Distinct equipment identities may be legitimate. No merge is recommended automatically.

Where names live today

  • Vendor master: vendors.name/business_name are text on an ID-based master. vendor_aliases stores canonical_name/alias as strings, not a vendor foreign key.
  • Vendor bills/rate cards/purchase orders: text vendor_name plus nullable vendors.id references. Text snapshots still exist independently of reviewed master linkage. hire_statements.vendor_name and equipment_master.vendor_name are text.
  • Diesel purchases: purchase details are on diesel_requirements, including supplier text; there is no separate diesel-purchase vendor master reference on that record.
  • Bulk material receipts: material_receipts.material_id refers to the plant material master operationally; supplier/transporter remain text. These material_id declarations do not all have database-enforced FKs.
  • Site trips: site_material_trips.material is text; supplier and material_source_supplier are separate text roles, each with an optional vendor master FK. Do not equate transporter and material seller.
  • Materials: plant_materials.name is an ID-based master, with aliases stored as JSON text. store_items is a separate ID-based stores master. Stocks/receipts/issues commonly hold material_id or item_id; store_issue_items also permits material_text fallback.
  • Purchasing: purchase_indent_items has description/vendor text plus optional material_id/vendor_id; PI item history/transactions retain vendor text. store_grns.supplier is text; GRN items reference store item IDs.
  • Other text/snapshots: material_logs, plant_production, site_purchases, RMC receipts, BOQ/SNL material resources, pending receipts and site_requirements JSON retain names outside a single canonical master. Vendor bill line descriptions are text, not a universal material FK.

Name transformations already present — reported, not changed

  • shared/businessText.ts:8–14 trims, collapses internal whitespace, then uppercases. Used on material/party/equipment master names and vendor-bill persistence.
  • server/vendor-master.ts:11–12 trims and uppercases vendor name/businessName (including imports using the schema). Other contact fields have separate trim rules.
  • VendorBills.tsx submits uppercase vendorName at2106 and2181; storage persists via uppercaseBusinessText at17675,17849,17910. These old bill paths are unchanged.
  • Legacy rate-card upsert normalizes matching vendor/key/unit with uppercase+trim and inserts uppercased vendor/key. The new setup does NOT call this method.
  • Material master create/update: storage5539–5558 uses uppercaseBusinessText. Purchase-order/material flows can create master names from uppercaseBusinessText(item.description) at15723/15737; this pre-existing behavior was not run or changed.
  • Material receipts create/update: storage5954–5955,6078–6079 uppercase supplier/transporter. DieselRequirements.tsx:1014 uppercases purchase supplier; storage updateDieselRequirement uppercases supplier.
  • DPR material supplier persistence uppercases at storage3482,4177,4555,4865. SiteEntry supplier inputs uppercase as typed.
  • SiteMaterialTrips and SiteMaterialsReceived uppercase supplier/material-source supplier as typed, with trims in edit/bulk payloads. ActivityReceiptStrip trims supplier on submission and uppercases supplier input.
  • PurchaseIndents GRN supplier is trimmed; RmcRawMaterials materialName is trimmed; BOQ recipe materialName is trimmed. Store import material strings are uppercased.
  • Alias resolution, candidate discovery, search filters and display also uppercase/trim. Those comparisons do not themselves rename stored rows; distinguish them from the ingress operations above.

The appendix includes all 2186 explicit uppercasing/trimming source locations across client/src, server and shared, including generic helpers and read/display/validation uses so they are not silently omitted. The name-context subset below is a review aid, not a claim that every match writes to the database. Importers/dynamic JSON and database snapshots need explicit mapping choices; no Tally mapping is built.

// Task #490 — Convert an LDO material receipt quantity to litres using the same
// logic as convertLdoToL() on the frontend (PlantLdoFlowMeter.tsx).
function convertLdoQtyToLiters(quantity: number, uom: string): number {
  const u = uom.toLowerCase().trim();
  if (u === "liters" || u === "litres" || u === "l") return quantity;
  if (u === "kg") return quantity / LDO_DENSITY_KG_PER_LITER;
  if (u === "mt" || u === "ton" || u === "tons" || u === "t") return (quantity * 1000) / LDO_DENSITY_KG_PER_LITER;
